--------------

**** Footnotes
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: footnotes
:CLASS: footnotes-heading
:END:
***** [[#DOCF1][(1)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you do not use Font Lock globally turn it on in Org buffer with
‘=(add-hook 'org-mode-hook #'turn-on-font-lock)='.

***** [[#DOCF2][(2)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-1
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Please consider subscribing to the mailing list in order to minimize the
work the mailing list moderators have to do.

***** [[#DOCF3][(3)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-2
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See the variables =org-special-ctrl-a/e=, =org-special-ctrl-k=, and
=org-ctrl-k-protect-subtree= to configure special behavior of C-a, C-e,
and C-k in headlines. Note also that clocking only works with headings
indented less than 30 stars.

***** [[#DOCF4][(4)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-3
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See, however, the option =org-cycle-emulate-tab=.

***** [[#DOCF5][(5)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-4
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The indirect buffer contains the entire buffer, but is narrowed to the
current tree. Editing the indirect buffer also changes the original
buffer, but without affecting visibility in that buffer. For more
information about indirect buffers, see
[[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_mono/emacs.html#Indirect-Buffers][GNU Emacs Manual]].

***** [[#DOCF6][(6)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-5
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When =org-agenda-inhibit-startup= is non-=nil=, Org does not honor the
default visibility state when first opening a file for the agenda (see
[[#Speeding-Up-Your-Agendas][Speeding Up Your Agendas]]).

***** [[#DOCF7][(7)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-6
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See also the variable =org-show-context-detail= to decide how much
context is shown around each match.

***** [[#DOCF8][(8)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-7
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This depends on the option =org-remove-highlights-with-change=.

***** [[#DOCF9][(9)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-8
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When using ‘=*=' as a bullet, lines must be indented so that they are
not interpreted as headlines. Also, when you are hiding leading stars to
get a clean outline view, plain list items starting with a star may be
hard to distinguish from true headlines. In short: even though ‘=*=' is
supported, it may be better to not use it for plain list items.

***** [[#DOCF10][(10)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-9
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can filter out any of them by configuring
=org-plain-list-ordered-item-terminator=.

***** [[#DOCF11][(11)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-10
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can also get ‘=a.=', ‘=A.=', ‘=a)=' and ‘=A)=' by configuring
=org-list-allow-alphabetical=. To minimize confusion with normal text,
those are limited to one character only. Beyond that limit, bullets
automatically become numbers.

***** [[#DOCF12][(12)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-11
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If there's a checkbox in the item, the cookie must be put /before/ the
checkbox. If you have activated alphabetical lists, you can also use
counters like ‘=[@b]='.

***** [[#DOCF13][(13)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-12
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you do not want the item to be split, customize the variable
=org-M-RET-may-split-line=.

***** [[#DOCF14][(14)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-13
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you want to cycle around items that way, you may customize
=org-list-use-circular-motion=.

***** [[#DOCF15][(15)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-14
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See =org-list-use-circular-motion= for a cyclic behavior.

***** [[#DOCF16][(16)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-15
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Many desktops intercept M-TAB to switch windows. Use C-M-i or ESC TAB
instead.

***** [[#DOCF17][(17)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-16
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
To insert a vertical bar into a table field, use ‘=\vert=' or, inside a
word ‘=abc\vert{}def='.

***** [[#DOCF18][(18)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-17
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Org understands references typed by the user as ‘=B4=', but it does not
use this syntax when offering a formula for editing. You can customize
this behavior using the variable =org-table-use-standard-references=.

***** [[#DOCF19][(19)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-18
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The computation time scales as O(N^2) because table =FOO= is parsed for
each field to be copied.

***** [[#DOCF20][(20)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-19
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The file ‘=constants.el=' can supply the values of constants in two
different unit systems, ‘=SI=' and ‘=cgs='. Which one is used depends on
the value of the variable =constants-unit-system=. You can use the
‘=STARTUP=' options ‘=constSI=' and ‘=constcgs=' to set this value for
the current buffer.

***** [[#DOCF21][(21)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-20
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The printf reformatting is limited in precision because the value passed
to it is converted into an “integer” or “double”. The “integer” is
limited in size by truncating the signed value to 32 bits. The “double”
is limited in precision to 64 bits overall which leaves approximately 16
significant decimal digits.

***** [[#DOCF22][(22)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-21
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Such names must start with an alphabetic character and use only
alphanumeric/underscore characters.

***** [[#DOCF23][(23)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-22
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Plain URIs are recognized only for a well-defined set of schemes. See
[[#External-Links][External Links]]. Unlike URI syntax, they cannot
contain parenthesis or white spaces, either. URIs within angle brackets
have no such limitation.

***** [[#DOCF24][(24)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-23
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
More accurately, the precise behavior depends on how point arrived
there---see
[[https://www.gnu.org/software/emacs/manual/html_mono/elisp.html#Invisible-Text][Invisible Text]].

***** [[#DOCF25][(25)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-24
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
To insert a link targeting a headline, in-buffer completion can be used.
Just type a star followed by a few optional letters into the buffer and
press M-TAB. All headlines in the current buffer are offered as
completions.

***** [[#DOCF26][(26)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-25
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When targeting a ‘=NAME=' keyword, the ‘=CAPTION=' keyword is mandatory
in order to get proper numbering (see [[#Captions][Captions]]).

***** [[#DOCF27][(27)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-26
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The actual behavior of the search depends on the value of the variable
=org-link-search-must-match-exact-headline=. If its value is =nil=, then
a fuzzy text search is done. If it is =t=, then only the exact headline
is matched, ignoring spaces and statistic cookies. If the value is
=query-to-create=, then an exact headline is searched; if it is not
found, then the user is queried to create it.

***** [[#DOCF28][(28)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-27
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The Org Id library must first be loaded, either through =org-customize=,
by enabling =id= in =org-modules=, or by adding ‘=(require 'org-id)=' in
your Emacs init file.

***** [[#DOCF29][(29)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-28
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Also, =org-link-context-for-files= and =org-id-link-use-context= should
be both enabled (which they are, by default).

***** [[#DOCF30][(30)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-29
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note that you do not have to use this command to insert a link. Links in
Org are plain text, and you can type or paste them straight into the
buffer. By using this command, the links are automatically enclosed in
double brackets, and you will be asked for the optional descriptive
text.

***** [[#DOCF31][(31)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-30
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
After insertion of a stored link, the link will be removed from the list
of stored links. To keep it in the list for later use, use a triple C-u
prefix argument to C-c C-l, or configure the option
=org-link-keep-stored-after-insertion=.

***** [[#DOCF32][(32)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-31
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This works if a function has been defined in the =:complete= property of
a link in =org-link-parameters=.

***** [[#DOCF33][(33)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-32
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See the variable =org-link-use-indirect-buffer-for-internals=.

***** [[#DOCF34][(34)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-33
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For backward compatibility, line numbers can also follow a single colon.

***** [[#DOCF35][(35)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-34
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Of course, you can make a document that contains only long lists of TODO
items, but this is not required.

***** [[#DOCF36][(36)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-35
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Changing the variable =org-todo-keywords= only becomes effective after
restarting Org mode in a buffer.

***** [[#DOCF37][(37)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-36
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This is also true for the t command in the agenda buffer.

***** [[#DOCF38][(38)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-37
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
All characters are allowed except ‘=@=', ‘=^=' and ‘=!=', which have a
special meaning here.

***** [[#DOCF39][(39)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-38
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Org mode parses these lines only when Org mode is activated after
visiting a file. C-c C-c with point in a line starting with ‘=#+=' is
simply restarting Org mode for the current buffer.

***** [[#DOCF40][(40)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-39
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The corresponding in-buffer setting is: ‘=#+STARTUP: logdone='.

***** [[#DOCF41][(41)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-40
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The corresponding in-buffer setting is: ‘=#+STARTUP: lognotedone='.

***** [[#DOCF42][(42)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-41
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See the variable =org-log-states-order-reversed=.

***** [[#DOCF43][(43)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-42
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note that the ‘=LOGBOOK=' drawer is unfolded when pressing SPC in the
agenda to show an entry---use C-u SPC to keep it folded here.

***** [[#DOCF44][(44)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-43
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
It is possible that Org mode records two timestamps when you are using
both =org-log-done= and state change logging. However, it never prompts
for two notes: if you have configured both, the state change recording
note takes precedence and cancel the closing note.

***** [[#DOCF45][(45)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-44
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See also the option =org-priority-start-cycle-with-default=.

***** [[#DOCF46][(46)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-45
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
To keep subtasks out of the global TODO list, see the option
=org-agenda-todo-list-sublevels=.

***** [[#DOCF47][(47)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-46
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
With the exception of description lists. But you can allow it by
modifying =org-list-automatic-rules= accordingly.

***** [[#DOCF48][(48)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-47
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Set the variable =org-checkbox-hierarchical-statistics= if you want such
cookies to count all checkboxes below the cookie, not just those
belonging to direct children.

***** [[#DOCF49][(49)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-48
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
C-u C-c C-c on the /first/ item of a list with no checkbox adds
checkboxes to the rest of the list.

***** [[#DOCF50][(50)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-49
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
As with all these in-buffer settings, pressing C-c C-c activates any
changes in the line.

***** [[#DOCF51][(51)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-50
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
To extend this default list to all tags used in all agenda files (see
[[#Agenda-Views][Agenda Views]]), customize the variable
=org-complete-tags-always-offer-all-agenda-tags=.

***** [[#DOCF52][(52)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-51
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Keys are automatically assigned to tags that have no configured keys.

***** [[#DOCF53][(53)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-52
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For both ‘=TIMESTAMP=' and ‘=TIMESTAMP_IA=': the word “first” refers to
the first occurrence in the entry, not the earliest in time; the prefix
‘=CLOCK:=' at the beginning of a clock entry is considered a keyword in
this context; and timestamps inside property drawers are ignored.

***** [[#DOCF54][(54)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-53
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If more than one summary type applies to the same property, the parent
values are computed according to the first of them.

***** [[#DOCF55][(55)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-54
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
An age can be defined as a duration, using units defined in
=org-duration-units=, e.g., ‘=3d 1h='. If any value in the column is as
such, the summary is also expressed as a duration.

***** [[#DOCF56][(56)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-55
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Please note that the ‘=COLUMNS=' definition must be on a single line; it
is wrapped here only because of formatting constraints.

***** [[#DOCF57][(57)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-56
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Contributed packages are not part of Emacs, but are distributed with the
main distribution of Org---visit [[https://orgmode.org]].

***** [[#DOCF58][(58)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-57
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The Org date format is inspired by the standard ISO 8601 date/time
format. To use an alternative format, see
[[#Custom-time-format][Custom time format]]. The day name is optional
when you type the date yourself. However, any date inserted or modified
by Org adds that day name, for reading convenience.

***** [[#DOCF59][(59)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-58
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When working with the standard diary expression functions, you need to
be very careful with the order of the arguments. That order depends
evilly on the variable =calendar-date-style=. For example, to specify a
date December 1, 2005, the call might look like
‘=(diary-date 12 1 2005)=' or ‘=(diary-date 1 12 2005)=' or
‘=(diary-date 2005 12 1)=', depending on the settings. This has been the
source of much confusion. Org mode users can resort to special versions
of these functions, namely =org-date=, =org-anniversary=, =org-cyclic=,
and =org-block=. These work just like the corresponding =diary-=
functions, but with stable ISO order of arguments (year, month, day)
wherever applicable, independent of the value of =calendar-date-style=.

***** [[#DOCF60][(60)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-59
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See the variable =org-read-date-prefer-future=. You may set that
variable to the symbol =time= to even make a time before now shift the
date to tomorrow.

***** [[#DOCF61][(61)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-60
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you do not need/want the calendar, configure the variable
=org-popup-calendar-for-date-prompt=.

***** [[#DOCF62][(62)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-61
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can also use the calendar command . to jump to today's date, but if
you are inserting an hour specification for your timestamp, . will then
insert a dot after the hour. By contrast, C-. will always jump to
today's date.

***** [[#DOCF63][(63)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-62
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you find this distracting, turn off the display with
=org-read-date-display-live=.

***** [[#DOCF64][(64)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-63
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
It will still be listed on that date after it has been marked as done.
If you do not like this, set the variable
=org-agenda-skip-scheduled-if-done=.

***** [[#DOCF65][(65)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-64
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The ‘=SCHEDULED=' and ‘=DEADLINE=' dates are inserted on the line right
below the headline. Do not put any text between this line and the
headline.

***** [[#DOCF66][(66)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-65
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note the corresponding ‘=STARTUP=' options ‘=logredeadline=',
‘=lognoteredeadline=', and ‘=nologredeadline='.

***** [[#DOCF67][(67)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-66
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note the corresponding ‘=STARTUP=' options ‘=logreschedule=',
‘=lognotereschedule=', and ‘=nologreschedule='.

***** [[#DOCF68][(68)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-67
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Org does not repeat inactive timestamps, however. See
[[#Timestamps][Timestamps]].

***** [[#DOCF69][(69)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-68
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
In fact, the target state is taken from, in this sequence, the
‘=REPEAT_TO_STATE=' property, the variable =org-todo-repeat-to-state= if
it is a string, the previous TODO state if =org-todo-repeat-to-state= is
=t=, or the first state of the TODO state sequence.

***** [[#DOCF70][(70)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-69
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can change this using the option =org-log-repeat=, or the
‘=STARTUP=' options ‘=logrepeat=', ‘=lognoterepeat=', and
‘=nologrepeat='. With ‘=lognoterepeat=', you will also be prompted for a
note.

***** [[#DOCF71][(71)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-70
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Clocking only works if all headings are indented with less than 30
stars. This is a hard-coded limitation of =lmax= in =org-clock-sum=.

***** [[#DOCF72][(72)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-71
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
To resume the clock under the assumption that you have worked on this
task while outside Emacs, use ‘=(setq org-clock-persist t)='.

***** [[#DOCF73][(73)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-72
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
To add an effort estimate “on the fly”, hook a function doing this to
=org-clock-in-prepare-hook=.

***** [[#DOCF74][(74)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-73
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The last reset of the task is recorded by the ‘=LAST_REPEAT=' property.

***** [[#DOCF75][(75)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-74
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See also the variable =org-clock-mode-line-total=.

***** [[#DOCF76][(76)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-75
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The corresponding in-buffer setting is: ‘=#+STARTUP: lognoteclock-out='.

***** [[#DOCF77][(77)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-76
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When using =:step=, =untilnow= starts from the beginning of 2003, not
the beginning of time.

***** [[#DOCF78][(78)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-77
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Language terms can be set through the variable
=org-clock-clocktable-language-setup=.

***** [[#DOCF79][(79)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-78
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note that all parameters must be specified in a single line---the line
is broken here only to fit it into the manual.

***** [[#DOCF80][(80)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-79
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
On computers using macOS, idleness is based on actual user idleness, not
just Emacs's idle time. For X11, you can install a utility program
‘=x11idle.c=', available in the ‘=org-contrib/=' repository, or install
the xprintidle package and set it to the variable
=org-clock-x11idle-program-name= if you are running Debian, to get the
same general treatment of idleness. On other systems, idle time refers
to Emacs idle time only.

***** [[#DOCF81][(81)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-80
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Please note the pitfalls of summing hierarchical data in a flat list
(see [[#Agenda-Column-View][Using Column View in the Agenda]]).

***** [[#DOCF82][(82)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-81
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note the corresponding ‘=STARTUP=' options ‘=logrefile=',
‘=lognoterefile=', and ‘=nologrefile='.

***** [[#DOCF83][(83)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-82
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Org used to offer four different targets for date/week tree capture.
Now, Org automatically translates these to use =file+olp+datetree=,
applying the =:time-prompt= and =:tree-type= properties. Please rewrite
your date/week-tree targets using =file+olp+datetree= since the older
targets are now deprecated.

***** [[#DOCF84][(84)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-83
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
A date tree is an outline structure with years on the highest level,
months or ISO weeks as sublevels and then dates on the lowest level.

#+begin_src example-preformatted
,* 2022
,** 2022-10 October
,*** 2022-10-07 Friday
,*** 2022-10-08 Saturday
#+end_src

TODO state, priority, tags, statistics cookies, and COMMENT keywords are
allowed in the tree structure.

***** [[#DOCF85][(85)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-84
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When the file name is not absolute, Org assumes it is relative to
=org-directory=.

***** [[#DOCF86][(86)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-85
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you need one of these sequences literally, escape the ‘=%=' with a
backslash.

***** [[#DOCF87][(87)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-86
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you define your own link types (see
[[#Adding-Hyperlink-Types][Adding Hyperlink Types]]), any property you
store with =org-store-link-props= can be accessed in capture templates
in a similar way.

***** [[#DOCF88][(88)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-87
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This is always the other, not the user. See the variable
=org-link-from-user-regexp=.

***** [[#DOCF89][(89)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-88
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you move entries or Org files from one directory to another, you may
want to configure =org-attach-id-dir= to contain an absolute path.

***** [[#DOCF90][(90)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-89
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If the value of that variable is not a list, but a single file name,
then the list of agenda files in maintained in that external file.

***** [[#DOCF91][(91)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-90
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When using the dispatcher, pressing < before selecting a command
actually limits the command to the current file, and ignores
=org-agenda-files= until the next dispatcher command.

***** [[#DOCF92][(92)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-91
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For backward compatibility, you can also press 1 to restrict to the
current buffer.

***** [[#DOCF93][(93)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-92
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For backward compatibility, the universal prefix argument C-u causes all
TODO entries to be listed before the agenda. This feature is deprecated,
use the dedicated TODO list, or a block agenda instead (see
[[#Block-agenda][Block agenda]]).

***** [[#DOCF94][(94)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-93
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The variable =org-anniversary= used in the example is just like
=diary-anniversary=, but the argument order is always according to ISO
and therefore independent of the value of =calendar-date-style=.

***** [[#DOCF95][(95)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-94
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you quote alphanumeric characters or underscores with a backslash,
that backslash is ignored.

***** [[#DOCF96][(96)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-95
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can, however, disable this by setting
=org-agenda-search-headline-for-time= variable to a =nil= value.

***** [[#DOCF97][(97)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-96
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Custom agenda commands can preset a filter by binding one of the
variables =org-agenda-tag-filter-preset=,
=org-agenda-category-filter-preset=, =org-agenda-effort-filter-preset=
or =org-agenda-regexp-filter-preset= as an option. This filter is then
applied to the view and persists as a basic filter through refreshes and
more secondary filtering. The filter is a global property of the entire
agenda view---in a block agenda, you should only set this in the global
options section, not in the section of an individual block.

***** [[#DOCF98][(98)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-97
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Only tags filtering is respected here, effort filtering is ignored.

***** [[#DOCF99][(99)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-98
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can also create persistent custom functions through
=org-agenda-bulk-custom-functions=.

***** [[#DOCF100][(100)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-99
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This file is parsed for the agenda when =org-agenda-include-diary= is
set.

***** [[#DOCF101][(101)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-100
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can provide a description for a prefix key by inserting a cons cell
with the prefix and the description.

***** [[#DOCF102][(102)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-101
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
/Planned/ means here that these entries have some planning information
attached to them, like a timestamp, a scheduled or a deadline string.
See =org-agenda-entry-types= on how to set what planning information is
taken into account.

***** [[#DOCF103][(103)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-102
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For HTML you need to install Hrvoje Nikšić's ‘=htmlize.el=' as an Emacs
package from [[https://elpa.nongnu.org/][NonGNU ELPA]] or from
[[https://github.com/hniksic/emacs-htmlize][Hrvoje Nikšić's repository]].

***** [[#DOCF104][(104)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-103
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
To create PDF output, the Ghostscript ps2pdf utility must be installed
on the system. Selecting a PDF file also creates the postscript file.

***** [[#DOCF105][(105)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-104
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If you want to store standard views like the weekly agenda or the global
TODO list as well, you need to define custom commands for them in order
to be able to specify file names.

***** [[#DOCF106][(106)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-105
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Quoting depends on the system you use, please check the FAQ for
examples.

***** [[#DOCF107][(107)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-106
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The markup will still be recognized. Just not highlighted visually in
Emacs.

***** [[#DOCF108][(108)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-107
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The underlying markup still remains a sub/superscript. Only the visual
display and export behavior changes.

***** [[#DOCF109][(109)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-108
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You can turn this on by default by setting the variable
=org-pretty-entities=, or on a per-file base with the ‘=STARTUP=' option
‘=entitiespretty='.

***** [[#DOCF110][(110)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-109
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This behavior can be disabled with ‘=-=' export setting (see
[[#Export-Settings][Export Settings]]).

***** [[#DOCF111][(111)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-110
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
LaTeX is a macro system based on Donald E. Knuth's TeX system. Many of
the features described here as “LaTeX” are really from TeX, but for
simplicity I am blurring this distinction.

***** [[#DOCF112][(112)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-111
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
When MathJax is used, only the environments recognized by MathJax are
processed. When dvipng, dvisvgm, or ImageMagick suite is used to create
images, any LaTeX environment is handled.

***** [[#DOCF113][(113)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-112
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
These are respectively available at
[[https://sourceforge.net/projects/dvipng/]],
[[http://dvisvgm.bplaced.net/]] and from the ImageMagick suite. Choose
the converter by setting the variable
=org-preview-latex-default-process= accordingly.

***** [[#DOCF114][(114)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-113
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Org mode has a method to test if point is inside such a fragment, see
the documentation of the function =org-inside-LaTeX-fragment-p=.

***** [[#DOCF115][(115)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-114
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This works automatically for the HTML backend (it requires version 1.34
of the ‘=htmlize.el=' package, which you need to install). Fontified
code chunks in LaTeX can be achieved using either the
[[https://www.ctan.org/pkg/listings][listings]] LaTeX package,
[[https://www.ctan.org/pkg/minted][minted]] LaTeX package, or by using
[[https://elpa.gnu.org/packages/engrave-faces.html][engrave-faces]] .
Refer to =org-latex-src-block-backend= for details.

***** [[#DOCF116][(116)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-115
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Source code in code blocks may also be evaluated either interactively or
on export. See [[#Working-with-Source-Code][Working with Source Code]]
for more information on evaluating code blocks.

***** [[#DOCF117][(117)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-116
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
In the ‘=src=' snippets, switches must be placed right after the
language name and before the
[[#Structure-of-Code-Blocks][header arguments]]

***** [[#DOCF118][(118)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-117
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This requires some Javascript which is /not/ automatically included in
the HTML output: you have to customize the variable
‘=org-html-head-include-scripts=' to =t= to have it included (it is
=nil= by default).

***** [[#DOCF119][(119)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-118
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Adding ‘=-k=' to ‘=-n -r=' /keeps/ the labels in the source code while
using line numbers for the links, which might be useful to explain those
in an Org mode example code.

***** [[#DOCF120][(120)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-119
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
You may select a different mode with the variable
=org-edit-fixed-width-region-mode=.

***** [[#DOCF121][(121)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-120
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
What Emacs considers to be an image depends on
=image-file-name-extensions= and =image-file-name-regexps=.

***** [[#DOCF122][(122)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-121
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The variable =org-startup-with-inline-images= can be set within a buffer
with the ‘=STARTUP=' options ‘=inlineimages=' and ‘=noinlineimages='.

***** [[#DOCF123][(123)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-122
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The width can be customized in Emacs >= 24.1, built with imagemagick
support.

***** [[#DOCF124][(124)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-123
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The corresponding in-buffer setting is: ‘=#+STARTUP: fninline=' or
‘=#+STARTUP: nofninline='.

***** [[#DOCF125][(125)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-124
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The corresponding in-buffer options are ‘=#+STARTUP: fnadjust=' and
‘=#+STARTUP: nofnadjust='.

***** [[#DOCF126][(126)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-125
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Many desktops intercept M-TAB to switch windows. Use C-M-i or ESC TAB
instead.

***** [[#DOCF127][(127)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-126
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The variable =org-export-date-timestamp-format= defines how this
timestamp are exported.

***** [[#DOCF128][(128)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-127
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For export to LaTeX format---or LaTeX-related formats such as Beamer---,
the ‘=org-latex-package-alist=' variable needs further configuration.
See [[#LaTeX-specific-export-settings][LaTeX specific export settings]].

***** [[#DOCF129][(129)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-128
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
At the moment, some export backends do not obey this specification. For
example, LaTeX export excludes every unnumbered headline from the table
of contents.

***** [[#DOCF130][(130)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-129
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note that =org-link-search-must-match-exact-headline= is locally bound
to non-=nil=. Therefore, =org-link-search= only matches headlines and
named elements.

***** [[#DOCF131][(131)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-130
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Since commas separate the arguments, commas within arguments have to be
escaped with the backslash character. So only those backslash characters
before a comma need escaping with another backslash character.

***** [[#DOCF132][(132)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-131
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For a less drastic behavior, consider using a select tag (see
[[#Export-Settings][Export Settings]]) instead.

***** [[#DOCF133][(133)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-132
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If ‘=BEAMER_ENV=' is set, Org export adds ‘=B_environment=' tag to make
it visible. The tag serves as a visual aid and has no semantic
relevance.

***** [[#DOCF134][(134)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-133
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
By default, Org loads MathJax from
[[https://www.jsdelivr.com/][jsDelivr]], as recommended in
[[https://docs.mathjax.org/en/latest/web/start.html][Getting Started with MathJax Components]].

***** [[#DOCF135][(135)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-134
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Please note that exported formulas are part of an HTML document, and
that signs such as ‘=<=', ‘=>=', or ‘=&=' have special meanings. See
[[https://docs.mathjax.org/en/latest/input/tex/html.html#tex-and-latex-in-html-documents][MathJax TeX and LaTeX in HTML documents]].

***** [[#DOCF136][(136)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-135
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If the classes on TODO keywords and tags lead to conflicts, use the
variables =org-html-todo-kwd-class-prefix= and
=org-html-tag-class-prefix= to make them unique.

***** [[#DOCF137][(137)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-136
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The command will open a PDF file, which is also available for download
from [[https://mirrors.ctan.org/info/latex-doc-ptr/latex-doc-ptr.pdf]]

***** [[#DOCF138][(138)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-137
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This does not allow setting different bibliography compilers for
different files. However, “smart” LaTeX compilation systems, such as
latexmk, can select the correct bibliography compiler.

***** [[#DOCF139][(139)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-138
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Minted uses an external Python package for code highlighting, which
requires the flag ‘=-shell-escape=' to be added to
=org-latex-pdf-process=.

***** [[#DOCF140][(140)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-139
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See
[[https://docs.oasis-open.org/office/v1.2/OpenDocument-v1.2.html][Open Document Format for Office Applications (OpenDocument) Version 1.2]].

***** [[#DOCF141][(141)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-140
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:

***** [[#DOCF146][(146)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-145
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Diary sexp events, except certain built-in types (see
=icalendar-export-sexp-enumerate-all=), are exported up to
=icalendar-export-sexp-enumeration-days= into future.

***** [[#DOCF147][(147)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-146
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Unless otherwise specified, each step of the export process only
operates on the accessible portion of the buffer. When subtree export is
selected (see [[#The-Export-Dispatcher][The Export Dispatcher]]), the
buffer is narrowed to the body of the selected subtree, so that the rest
of the buffer text, except export keywords, does not contribute to the
export output.

***** [[#DOCF148][(148)]]

:END:
See transcoders and =:translate-alist= in the docstrings of
=org-export-define-backend= and =org-export-define-derived-backend=.

***** [[#DOCF149][(149)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-148
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
See =inner-template= in the docstring of =org-export-define-backend=.

***** [[#DOCF150][(150)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-149
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If the publishing directory is the same as the source directory,
‘=file.org=' is exported as ‘=file.org.org=', so you probably do not
want to do this.

***** [[#DOCF151][(151)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-150
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The option =org-babel-no-eval-on-ctrl-c-ctrl-c= can be used to remove
code evaluation from the C-c C-c key binding.

***** [[#DOCF152][(152)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-151
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Actually, the constructs ‘=call_<name>()=' and ‘=src_<lang>{}=' are not
evaluated when they appear in a keyword (see
[[#In_002dbuffer-Settings][Summary of In-Buffer Settings]]).

***** [[#DOCF153][(153)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-152
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Actually, the constructs ‘=call_<name>()=' and ‘=src_<lang>{}=' are not
evaluated when they appear in a keyword (see
[[#In_002dbuffer-Settings][Summary of In-Buffer Settings]]).

***** [[#DOCF154][(154)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-153
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For noweb literate programming details, see
[[https://www.cs.tufts.edu/~nr/noweb/]].

***** [[#DOCF155][(155)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-154
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
In the following example, attempting to evaluate the second code block
will give an error, because the variables defined in the first code
block will not be defined in the second block.

#+begin_src example-preformatted
,#+NAME: get-prompt
,#+BEGIN_SRC emacs-lisp :var prompt="root> " :var command="ls"
  (concat prompt command)
,#+END_SRC
,#+RESULTS: get-prompt
: root> ls
,#+BEGIN_SRC emacs-lisp :noweb yes
  <<get-prompt>>
,#+END_SRC
#+end_src

The previous block is expanded without setting =prompt= and =command=
values.

#+begin_src example-preformatted
,#+BEGIN_SRC emacs-lisp
  (concat prompt command)
,#+END_SRC
#+end_src

***** [[#DOCF156][(156)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-155
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The reference is evaluated with point at the referenced block, using its
header arguments (including inherited)

***** [[#DOCF157][(157)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-156
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For more information, please refer to the commentary section in
‘=org-tempo.el='.

***** [[#DOCF158][(158)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-157
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Org Indent mode also sets =wrap-prefix= correctly for indenting and
wrapping long lines of headlines or text. This minor mode also handles
Visual Line mode and directly applied settings through =word-wrap=.

***** [[#DOCF159][(159)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-158
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
This works, but requires extra effort. Org Indent mode is more
convenient for most applications.

***** [[#DOCF160][(160)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-159
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
=org-adapt-indentation= can also be set to ‘='headline-data=', in which
case only data lines below the headline will be indented.

***** [[#DOCF161][(161)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-160
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note that Org Indent mode also sets the =wrap-prefix= property, such
that Visual Line mode (or purely setting =word-wrap=) wraps long lines,
including headlines, correctly indented.

***** [[#DOCF162][(162)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-161
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
For a server to host files, consider using a WebDAV server, such as
[[https://nextcloud.com][Nextcloud]]. Additional help is at this
[[https://orgmode.org/worg/org-faq.html#mobileorg_webdav][FAQ entry]].

***** [[#DOCF163][(163)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-162
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If Emacs is configured for safe storing of passwords, then configure the
variable =org-mobile-encryption-password=; please read the docstring of
that variable.

***** [[#DOCF164][(164)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-163
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Symbolic links in =org-directory= need to have the same name as their
targets.

***** [[#DOCF165][(165)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-164
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
While creating the agendas, Org mode forces ‘=ID=' properties on all
referenced entries, so that these entries can be uniquely identified if
Org Mobile flags them for further action. To avoid setting properties
configure the variable =org-mobile-force-id-on-agenda-items= to =nil=.
Org mode then relies on outline paths, assuming they are unique.

***** [[#DOCF166][(166)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-165
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Checksums are stored automatically in the file ‘=checksums.dat='.

***** [[#DOCF167][(167)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-166
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The file will be empty after this operation.

***** [[#DOCF168][(168)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-167
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
By default, =org-yank-dnd-default-attach-method= is set to nil -- use
the same value as =org-attach-method= (=cp= by default).

***** [[#DOCF169][(169)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-168
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
[[https://www.ctan.org/pkg/comment]]

***** [[#DOCF170][(170)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-169
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
By default this works only for LaTeX, HTML, and Texinfo. Configure the
variable =orgtbl-radio-table-templates= to install templates for other
modes.

***** [[#DOCF171][(171)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-170
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
If the ‘=TBLFM=' keyword contains an odd number of dollar characters,
this may cause problems with Font Lock in LaTeX mode. As shown in the
example you can fix this by adding an extra line inside the ‘=comment='
environment that is used to balance the dollar expressions. If you are
using AUCTeX with the font-latex library, a much better solution is to
add the ‘=comment=' environment to the variable
=LaTeX-verbatim-environments=.

***** [[#DOCF172][(172)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-171
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
The =agenda*= view is the same as =agenda= except that it only considers
/appointments/, i.e., scheduled and deadline items that have a time
specification ‘=[h]h:mm=' in their timestamps.

***** [[#DOCF173][(173)]]
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: section-172
:CLASS: footnote-body-heading
:END:
Note that, for =org-odd-levels-only=, a level number corresponds to
order in the hierarchy, not to the number of stars.
